town_stop_lines — DRIVE town op

• Data kinds: table → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.town_stop_lines(layout, *, side: 'str' = 'left') -> 'List[dict]' (to call the implementation directly, import drivetown; drivetown.town_stop_lines(layout, *, side: 'str' = 'left') -> 'List[dict]'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("town_stop_lines"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Lists the town's stop lines in order of arc length: [{"s", "x", "y", "yaw", "kind", "element", "crossing_zone": (s0, s1) | None, "drawn": bool}, ...].

Intersections: among the element's stop_lines (segments (2, 2)), the one whose endpoint lies on the centreline and which extends to the side of the direction of travel is the stop line of the driving path (1 of 4. For left-hand traffic the left one; for right-hand traffic the mirrored one). Railway crossings: the stop-line position is the closed form crossing surface − stop_setback (drivecourse draws the white line only in the left lane, so it does not depend on side. drawn = whether a white line is drawn on that side). s is the arc length along the centreline, yaw the direction of travel there. Railway crossings also get crossing_zone, the arc-length range of the crossing surface.

Raises ValueError: layout is not from town_chain, side is not left/right.
